newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower as frost concerns wane.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower as frost concerns wane.

text.p: Diminished concerns about severe damage to the U.S. soybean crop due to freezing temperatures this week drove CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"If we do not have to worry about the weather then the technicals will dominate and they (technicals) don't look good, especially with harvest coming on," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
About one-third of the corn and soybeans in Illinois, Iowa and Minnesota will be at risk if temperatures fall below freezing Thursday morning.
But agronomists expected frost damage to be light.
"Your absolute yield loss is not going to be all that great," said Don White, University of Illinois agronomist.

Traders said "some" damage probably would occur as a result of the cold weather. Meteorologists early Wednesday said a crop-killing freeze entered the western U.S. Midwest early Wednesday and should spread Thursday and early Friday across Iowa, northern Illinois, northern Indiana and northwest Ohio.
Soybeans closed two to 7-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down 7-1/4 at $7.42.

Refco Inc sold six million bushels of November and sold1.5 million of November 1997, the traders said. Term Commodities sold two million bushels of November, Dean Witter Reynolds sold one million November and Rand Financial sold two million November, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 85,000 contracts, down from 96,077 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 600 November $7.50 calls at 14-3/4 to 16 cents, Griffin Trading bought 1,000 January $7.25 puts at seven cents and Cargill Investor Services bought 400 November $7.75 calls at 6-1/2 to seven cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 27,000, down from 48,554 Tuesday.
